home.faq1A: Our AI models are trained on over 50 million labeled agricultural datasets and verified by certified agronomists. We maintain a 98.4% accuracy rate for major crop diseases and nutritional deficiencies when provided with clear images and local data.
home.faq2A: AgroAI currently supports over 120 different crops including major cereals (corn, wheat, rice), legumes, fruits, vegetables, and specialized cash crops like coffee and cocoa. We are constantly adding new varieties based on user feedback and regional needs.
home.faq3A: Your data privacy is our top priority. All uploaded information is encrypted and stored securely. We do not sell individual farmer data to third parties. Agronomic data is only used in an aggregated, anonymous format to improve the AI models for the benefit of the entire farming community.
home.faq4A: AgroAI is supported by a consortium of international agricultural NGOs and philanthropic foundations committed to global food security. Their sponsorship allows us to provide professional-grade tools to every farmer regardless of their operation's size.
home.testimonialQuote: When my paddy showed yellowing in the leaves, I tried AgroAI. Within minutes I got the diagnosis and a treatment plan in my language. It's free and works on my phone—exactly what small farmers like us needed.

diagnosis.title: Comprehensive Multi-Factor Diagnosis
diagnosis.subtitle: Upload multi-modal data including crop visuals, soil reports, and environmental context for maximum AI analysis accuracy.
diagnosis.aiProgressDesc: Our AI is analyzing the uploaded crop with the uploaded image evidence. We'll show you the full report shortly.
diagnosis.descriptionPlaceholder: Describe any symptoms, observations, or concerns about your crops. You can type or use the microphone to record your description...
diagnosis.voiceRecordingUnsupported: Voice recording requires Chrome, Edge, or Safari browser.
diagnosis.tipsReportTitle: Get the Best Yield from Your AI Report
diagnosis.reportTip1Title: Follow the action plan in order
diagnosis.reportTip1Desc: The report lists immediate and follow-up steps by priority. Following them in order helps recovery and maximizes yield.
diagnosis.reportTip2Desc: Check weather and soil factors in the report to plan irrigation, spraying, and crop protection at the right time.
diagnosis.reportTip3Desc: After 1–2 weeks, upload new photos to see progress and get updated recommendations for continued improvement.
diagnosis.weatherTipClear: Ideal for fieldwork and spraying. Plan outdoor tasks.
diagnosis.weatherTipPartlyCloudy: Good conditions for most crop activities.
diagnosis.weatherTipFog: Delay spraying; poor visibility. Check drainage in low areas.
diagnosis.weatherTipRain: High humidity after rain increases fungal risk. Check drainage.
diagnosis.weatherTipSnow: Protect sensitive crops. Avoid heavy field traffic.
diagnosis.weatherTipRainShowers: Unpredictable wet spells. Postpone pesticide application.
diagnosis.weatherTipSnowShowers: Frost risk. Cover or protect vulnerable plants.
diagnosis.weatherTipThunderstorm: Avoid field work. Secure equipment and structures.
diagnosis.weatherTipVariable: Check local conditions before planning field work.
diagnosis.weatherAlertDesc: High humidity following rain increases risk of fungal infections. Check drainage.
diagnosis.tip1Desc: Remove suckers from leaf axils to direct energy toward fruit and improve airflow.
diagnosis.tip2Desc: Tomatoes thrive in soil between 21-29°C. Use organic mulch to help regulate root temperature.
diagnosis.tip3Desc: Maintain even moisture to prevent blossom end rot and fruit cracking during fruit set.
